title: Exact Integer Range Materialization v1
objective: Preallocate and fill trusted built-in exact integer ranges for Sage ellipsis and list(range(...)) while preserving generic Python iteration fallbacks, reducing one-million-entry materialization below 80 ms with comprehensive conformance tests

handoff.summary: Added checked runtime primitives for preallocated exact-integer range materialization and lazy native exact-range iteration, routed built-in range iteration through the native iterator, and accelerated the common one- and two-start Sage ellipsis forms while retaining the existing generic fallback. CPython-differential tests cover iterator identity, next, exhaustion, fallback, repeated and nested iteration, and exact Number/BigInt transitions; Sage tests cover inclusive and descending ellipses, zero steps, oversized materialization, symbolic/rational/float fallbacks, richer prefixes, and iterator overrides. On this host [1..10^6] fell from about 538 ms to 6.57 ms median and list(range(1, 10^6 + 1)) measured 42.19 ms, both below the 80 ms gate. The integration lane added the runtime type signatures, registered the focused test, regenerated the reviewed native-boundary inventory, and validated the final combined tree with a production build, zero-error strict baselib checks, architecture checks, 119 unit tests, and 261 passing integration tests with one intentional capability skip.
risks: Sage ellipsis materialization briefly owns a raw preallocated array and its decorated-list copy; the observed one-million-entry path remains small and fast, but substantially larger lists retain ordinary JavaScript allocation limits.
